text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called a "silent killer" because it typically has no symptoms, and many people can have it for years without knowing it.

Symptoms usually do not show up unless blood pressure reaches dangerously high levels (a hypertensive crisis, typically 180/120 mm Hg or higher). In severe cases or during a crisis, signs may include:

list.snippet: Confusion, weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking (signs of a stroke or emergency)

text_blocks.snippet: According to the American Heart Association, if your blood pressure reading is higher than 180/120 mm Hg:

list.snippet: Wait one minute and take it again.
If it remains that high and you have emergency symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, vision changes, or difficulty speaking, call 911 immediately.
If it is 180/120 mm Hg or higher without symptoms, contact your healthcare provider right away.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about managing your numbers through the World Health Organization Hypertension Fact Sheet or the Cleveland Clinic Hypertension Guide.
